etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French rural, from Latin rūrālis (“rural”), from rūs (“countryside”) + -ālis.

definitions.definition: Relating to the countryside or to agriculture.

quote.citation: 1913, Robert Barr, chapter 4, in Lord Stranleigh Abroad‎[1]:
quote.text: Nothing could be more business-like than the construction of the stout dams, and nothing more gently rural than the limpid lakes, with the grand old forest trees marshalled round their margins … .

definitions.definition: (obsolete) A person from the countryside; a rustic.
